summary: A one-page personal site for an engineer, designer, consultant or freelancer, with numbered sections and a sticky identity column, plus the same content as a print-perfect A4 CV that saves as PDF.

pages.purpose: Everything on one page: who the person is, what they have done, what they have made and written, what they know and how to reach them.

sections.purpose: A sticky identity column on wide screens: name, role and location, current status, section links, 'Download PDF', profile links and language switch.
fields: Availability status (open to work / booked until)
CV file name for the PDF
sections.notes: The section links work as a table of contents: the item for the section being read gets aria-current="location"; without JavaScript they are plain in-page anchors. On narrow screens the column sits above the content and is not sticky. Number the sections (01, 02 …) in the accent.

sections.purpose: A two-or-three sentence introduction and what the person is doing right now.
fields: Introduction in the person's own voice

sections.purpose: Jobs as a timeline, newest first, the current one marked.
fields: What the employer does and where
Three or four achievement bullets with numbers where possible

sections.purpose: Selected projects with an outcome each, linking out.
alternatives: entity-card: card grid when projects have images

sections.purpose: Articles and talks: dated list with reading time, plus talks with event name.
alternatives: list-layout: a plain dated list of links to posts hosted elsewhere
fields: Post title, date, reading time, link

sections.purpose: Skills grouped by area, then languages spoken and education.
What kind of work the person is open to and how to reach them, with the CV download again.
alternatives: contact-form: when the person prefers a form to a public email address

pages.purpose: The same content as one sheet of A4 paper on screen, printing or saving as PDF without any site chrome.

sections.purpose: A slim bar with a link back to the site and 'Download PDF'.
sections.notes: 'Download PDF' opens the print dialog; swap the document title for the file name while it is open so 'Save as PDF' suggests a sensible name. Say in the button hint that it opens the print dialog.

sections.purpose: The CV sheet: name and contact header, experience, selected projects, skills, languages, education.
fields: Everything from the home page, in short form
sections.notes: Always light (paper is paper, also in dark mode); two columns that collapse on narrow screens; an @page rule for A4 with about 12 mm margins; break-inside: avoid on every entry; links printed as their visible address. The home page also carries a print-only copy so printing either page prints only the sheet.

content: Availability status and what kind of work is wanted
Work history: role, employer, dates, place, achievement bullets, tools
Selected projects with year, outcome and link
Contact email, optional phone and profile links

styles.name: plain engineer
styles.why: System type, mono dates and section numbers, one cool accent and almost no decoration: reads like well-kept documentation. Suits engineers and technical consultants.

styles.name: editorial profile
styles.why: Serif headings and generous measure for writers, researchers and designers who want the CV to feel like a printed page.

pitfalls: Printing the whole site instead of the CV: hide site chrome in print and print only the sheet, on A4 with real margins.
Dark mode leaking into the printed or on-screen CV sheet; keep the paper light and check it reads without colour.
Content that breaks across pages mid-entry; avoid breaks inside entries and keep the reading order logical when printed.
Publishing a full home address, date of birth, ID number or a personal phone number the person did not mean to make public.
Links that print as 'here': print the address itself so the PDF stays useful on paper.
The sticky identity column taking the whole screen on phones; it should stack above the content there.
Section navigation without aria-current, or scroll effects that ignore reduced motion.
